draft.title: Identifying bioethical issues
card: A bioethical issue arises when biology or medicine raises a question of right and wrong. Science can show what is possible, but it cannot alone say whether we should do it.
Gene editing is one example. Scientists can change the DNA of an organism, and people disagree about whether it is right to do so, especially in human embryos.
Cloning is another. Making a genetic copy of an animal is possible, and people ask whether it is right to do it and how the animals are treated.
A question about how something works, such as how many chromosomes a cell has, can be answered with evidence alone. It is not a bioethical issue.
draft.remember: A bioethical issue is a question of right and wrong that biology or medicine makes us ask.

a.q: Which of these is a bioethical issue?
opts: Whether it is right to edit genes in human embryos
How many chromosomes a human body cell contains
Which stage of mitosis comes after metaphase
How a clone's DNA compares with its parent's DNA
a.why: Whether editing human embryos is right is a question of right and wrong, so it is a bioethical issue. The other three can be answered with evidence alone, so they are not.
a.clue: Which question asks whether something should be done, not how it works?

b.q: A lab in Geelong can clone a prize sheep. Which question about this is a bioethical issue?
opts: Is it right to clone animals for profit
How many cells does the clone start from
Does the clone have the same DNA as the sheep
Which tools does the lab use to make the clone
b.why: Whether cloning for profit is right is a question of right and wrong. The other options ask about how cloning works or what it produces, and evidence can answer these. The DNA question is tempting because it is about cloning, but it is a factual question.
b.clue: A topic being about cloning is not enough. Look for a question of right and wrong.

a.best: Whether it is right to edit genes in human embryos

b.best: Is it right to clone animals for profit
